svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop
svg.desc: A static SVG educational interface that simulates drag-and-drop label placement with internal links, layered visibility, and popup panels.

g.text: Identify ten structures and connect each term to the diagram.
Select a word-bank tile to reveal its matching label layer.

g.aria-label: Vector illustration of a complete flower

g.text: Choose a label tile from the word bank.
The term appears in its matching slot.
Follow the arrow to identify the flower part.
Use the buttons below for support.
Pollen moves from an anther to a stigma, often with a pollinator.
Choose a tile to place it
• The pistil is the female reproductive organ.
• Its parts run from top to bottom: stigma → style → ovary.
• The stamen is the male reproductive organ.
• Each stamen has an anther supported by a filament.
• Sepals protect the bud, while the receptacle anchors the flower.
Showy petals attract pollinators; green sepals cover the developing bud.
Match the slot numbers to the structures below.
Petal — colorful blade that attracts pollinators
Sepal — leaflike protection at the base
Filament — slender stalk of the stamen
Receptacle — enlarged tip where parts attach
Style — stalk connecting stigma and ovary
Stigma — sticky tip that catches pollen
This clears the currently revealed label layer and closes this panel.
The diagram and word bank remain ready for another round.
